text: dsh-gitmodules-dir 是一个 DSH 插件，为 DSH 注册 Git 子模块管理工具和配套技能。它调用 vendored 的 git-partial-submodule 脚本，支持以 blobless 部分克隆添加子模块、克隆后初始化部分子模块，以及保存和恢复写在 .gitmodules 中的 sparse-checkout 模式。工具在会话工作目录或指定的超项目目录中执行，并返回退出码、标准输出和错误输出。适合希望减少子模块下载内容并在不同检出间保留稀疏路径配置的开发者。运行环境需要 git 2.27 或更高版本及 python3 3.8 或更高版本。

dsh-gitmodules-dir adds a Git submodule tool and skill to DSH. It can add blobless submodules, initialize them after cloning, and save or restore sparse-checkout patterns in .gitmodules. It runs in the session or specified project directory and needs git 2.27+ and python3 3.8+.

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · dsh-gitmodules-dir：git-partial-submodule bundle for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): lets dsh users add, clone, and manage
**partial git submodules** — blobless partial clones plus sparse checkout — without hand-rolling the
underlying git plumbing. It wraps the [git-partial-submodule](https://github.com/Reedbeta/git-partial-submodule)
project (Apache-2.0): the upstream single-file Python script is vendored into this bundle
(`bin/git-partial-submodule.py`, pinned to commit `bd8bb4e7`) and exposed to the model.

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · dsh-gitmodules-dir：| Layer | Source | Shape in dsh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool | Vendored [git-partial-submodule](https://github.com/Reedbeta/git-partial-submodule) script, run via `python3` | Built-in tool `git_partial_submodule` (add / clone / save-sparse / restore-sparse) |
| Skill | This bundle | Built-in skill `git-partial-submodule` in the model's `<available_skills>` catalog, loaded on demand via the `skill` tool |

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · Why partial submodules：In top-level repositories, git provides partial-clone options such as "blobless" clone to reduce the
burden of downloading large repositories, but for submodules only "shallow" clones are supported by
git, and shallow clones have usability issues. [git-partial-submodule](https://github.com/Reedbeta/git-partial-submodule)
clones submodules as blobless repos — fully functional while saving bandwidth and disk space — and
stores sparse-checkout patterns in `.gitmodules`, so they travel with the superproject under version
control.

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · What the model gets：- Tool `git_partial_submodule` — runs one git-partial-submodule operation in the session working
  directory (or an explicit `cwd`):
  - `add` — add a new submodule as a blobless partial clone (`-b`/`--branch`, `--name`, `--sparse`).
  - `clone` — initialize partial submodules after a fresh clone of the superproject, applying sparse
    patterns saved in `.gitmodules`.
  - `save-sparse` — persist the submodule's current sparse patterns to `.gitmodules`.
  - `restore-sparse` — reapply the sparse patterns saved in `.gitmodules` after pulls or branch
    switches.
- Skill `git-partial-submodule` — teaches when and how to use the operations, with the exact
  underlying command lines in `references/git-commands.md` (read on demand through the directory
  resource hint).

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · What the model gets：The tool returns `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }`; a non-zero `exitCode` means the operation failed —
the model reads `stderr` and reports it.

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · Syncing the vendored script：`bin/git-partial-submodule.py` is vendored from the upstream
[git-partial-submodule](https://github.com/Reedbeta/git-partial-submodule) repository pinned to a
commit, keeping "plugin version ↔ upstream version" reproducible:

```sh
npm run sync-script            # sync the pinned commit
npm run sync-script -- <ref>   # sync a specific commit / tag / branch
npm run smoke                  # end-to-end smoke test of the four operations
```

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- Partial clone and sparse checkout are still experimental git features that may have sharp edges.
- The tool works by fiddling with repository internals in not-officially-supported ways; it may fail
  or leave the repo in a bad state in edge cases.
- Recursive clone is not supported; not all options of the underlying `git clone` / `git submodule
  add` are supported; spaces in sparse-checkout patterns are not handled correctly.

dsh-gitmodules-dir README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- git >= 2.37 defaults to "cone" mode sparse checkout, where `git sparse-checkout list` returns
  empty. As a result `save-sparse` stores an empty pattern and `clone` / `restore-sparse` cannot
  re-apply sparse mode, because the upstream script supports non-cone mode only. Workaround: run the
  superproject's git with `core.sparseCheckoutCone=false` (e.g. `git config --global
  core.sparseCheckoutCone false`), or set sparse patterns explicitly with
  `git -C <sub> sparse-checkout set --no-cone ...`.
- `add --sparse` enables sparse checkout in the new submodule but does not write the initial pattern
  set to `.gitmodules` (an upstream TODO); run `save-sparse` once to persist it.
- `--filter` is ignored when the submodule repository is served over a plain local path; use a
  `file://` URL or a real remote (https) for the blobless filter to take effect.
